summary: Alexander Robertson worked in religious studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Aberdeen (M.A. ~1894–1898) and the University of Glasgow, and served as a missionary for the United Free Church of Scotland from 1902 to 1937.

Alexander Rogers worked in Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and history/archaeology. He studied at the East India Company College (~1842–1845) and served in the Indian Civil Service from 1845 to 1879.

Alexander Rödel is a scholar in religious studies and Indology. He earned a Master of Science by Research at the University of Edinburgh (attested 2008), where he studied under Steven Sutcliffe and Jeanne Openshaw.

Alexander Schiller is an Indology and history/archaeology scholar. He studied at Appalachian State University (BA 2010–2014), UC San Diego (MAS 2019–2021), and Kansas State University (PhD 2025), later joining the Bavarian Academy of Sciences and Humanities as Wissenschaftlicher Mitarbeiter (attested 2026).
Alexander Studholme is a scholar in Buddhist studies. He studied under Paul Williams and Rupert Gethin (~1996–2001).

Alexander W. Macdonald worked in Tibetology and religious studies. He held posts at the CNRS (~1957–1976), Musée de l'Homme (attested 1972), Kailash (~1973–1980), Paris Nanterre University (Professor ~1976–1991), and the University of Paris (attested 1982).
Alexander Walker worked in Indology and history/archaeology. He studied at the University of St Andrews (~1778–1780) and held a post with the East India Company (~1780–1812).

Alexander Wynne works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Bristol under Paul Williams and Rupert Gethin, and completed a DPhil at the University of Oxford (2000–2003) under Richard Gombrich, later serving as Junior Research Fellow at St John's College, Oxford (2002–2006).

Alexander Yiannopoulos is a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied at Ka-Nying Shedrub Ling and under numerous scholars including Karin Myers, Sherab Sangpo, Khenpo Sherab Dorje, Georges B. J. Dreyfus, Tom Tillemans, and Jay L. Garfield.

Alexander Zieseniss was an Indologist who studied at Heidelberg, Freiburg, Hamburg (PhD ~1925–1928), Tübingen, and Berlin, under scholars including Ernst Leumann and Walther Schubring. He habilitated at Hamburg (1936–1941) and served as Privatdozent at the University of Breslau (~1938–1945).

Alexander von Humboldt was active in history/archaeology and other fields. He studied at European University Viadrina, the University of Göttingen under Georg Forster and Christian Gottlob Heyne, Handelsakademie Hamburg, TU Bergakademie Freiberg, and the University of Jena (~1794–1797), where he also held a post.

Alexander von Rospatt works in Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of London and earned his PhD at the University of Hamburg under Lambert Schmithausen. He held posts at Leipzig and Vienna, and at UC Berkeley (attested 2011–2026).

Alexander von Staël-Holstein worked in Buddhist studies, Indology, and sinology. He studied at Tartu, Berlin, Halle-Wittenberg, and Saint Petersburg. His posts included Saint Petersburg State University (1909), Peking University (1918–1929), the Sino-Indian Institute (~1928–1937), and Harvard-Yenching Institute (from 1929).

Alexandra David-Néel worked in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. She studied at the Royal Conservatory of Brussels and the University of Paris, and under Sylvain Lévi, Philippe Édouard Foucaux, Swami Bhaskarananda Saraswati, Kazi Dawa Samdup, and Lachen Gomchen Rinpoche.

Alexandra van der Geer works in Indology and history/archaeology. She studied under scholars including Karel R. van Kooij, Leendert A. van Daalen, and Henk Bodewitz, and held a visiting post at the International Institute for Asian Studies.

Alexandre Langlois was an Indologist who studied under Antoine-Léonard Chézy. He served as Professor of Rhetorics at Lycée Charlemagne (~1826–1854), member of the Académie des Inscriptions et Belles-Lettres (1835–1854), and inspector at the Académie de Paris (~1835–1854).

Alexey Belyakov works in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Amur State University (2001–2010), later holding posts as archaeologist (2007–2013), senior researcher at Amur State University (2013–2017), and associate professor at Heihe University (2017–2018) and Changchun University (2018).
Alexis Cordier worked in Indology and Tibetology. He studied at the École de santé navale (~1890–1894) and earned his medical doctorate (Dr.med.) at the University of Bordeaux (~1890–1894).

Alexis Sanderson is a scholar of Indology, religious studies, and philosophy. He studied at Balliol College and the University of Oxford, and under Swami Lakshman Joo. He held posts at Merton, Brasenose, All Souls College, and the University of Oxford (~1977–2015).

Alf Hiltebeitel was an Indology and religious studies scholar. He studied at Haverford College and the University of Chicago under J. A. B. van Buitenen and Victor Turner, and held faculty posts at George Washington University from 1968 onward, becoming Columbian Professor in 1981.
